clue.text: Not vetoed," you say for all to hear

indicators.note: 'you say' marks that a word spoken is what counts, so the sound of the phrase gives the entry

parts.note: something not vetoed is permitted, i.e. allowed

explanation.surface: Someone declares publicly that a proposal has not been blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' signals that ALLOWED, the meaning of 'Not vetoed', is pronounced just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken audibly, so that everyone present can catch the words.

clue.text: In agreement with one over the child

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece written over another comes before it

parts.note: uni- is the prefix meaning one
a child of a parent is a son

explanation.surface: Agreeing with someone about the child.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places UNI above SON. 'In' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is complete accord, everyone acting or speaking as one.

clue.text: The servant, Nora, has fallen in a big way

indicators.note: something that has fallen is jumbled and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a maid is a female servant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A maidservant called Nora has tripped over on a large street.
explanation.walkthrough: MAID plus NORA are rearranged by 'has fallen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal road is a wide thoroughfare, a big way through a town.

clue.text: In a super manoeuvre the firm makes good its losses

indicators.note: 'In' puts the firm inside the rearranged word
a manoeuvre moves things around, so the letters of super are rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company recovers its losses with a brilliant business move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' turns SUPER into REUPS, and 'In' puts CO inside to give RE-CO-UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money lost, making good a deficit.

clue.text: A gun for the teller

definitions.meaning: a firearm that fires several shots without reloading
someone who tells something again, passing it on

explanation.definitionFit: A firearm firing successive shots, and also a person who passes on what they hear to others.

clue.text: As the patient is in hospital with the same old slipped disc?

definitions.text: As the patient is in hospital with the same old slipped disc?

parts.words: As the patient is in hospital with the same old slipped disc?
parts.note: a patient whose old spinal trouble has recurred has a sore spine once more and is returned to the ward once more: both senses of the phrase

explanation.surface: A patient is readmitted to hospital with a recurrent spinal problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means returned once more, and also describes a spine that hurts once more.

clue.text: Lengthens "The Lone Ranger" stage version

indicators.note: a ranger roams about, so the letters wander out of order
a new version of something is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre adaptation of the cowboy hero's story that drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: LONE plus STAGE are rearranged; both 'Ranger' and 'version' signal the shuffle, and 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something longer is to stretch it out.

clue.text: Was first, for instance, to be drawn into Prohibition

indicators.note: one piece is pulled inside another, so it sits within it

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Someone was the first to get caught up in the era of Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have started something is to have come at its start, been first.

clue.text: Be eager to get into a first-class hotel

indicators.note: the hotel letter gets into the other word, so it sits within it

parts.note: ace means excellent, first-class
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Wanting badly to check into a luxury hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside ACE. 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Meets and makes an impact on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to encounter unexpectedly and to crash into.

clue.text: Stops and sees that everything's all right

explanation.definitionFit: To halt or restrain something, and to inspect it to verify it is in order.

clue.text: With open wounds, has internal injuries

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and reshaped, so they are rearranged
only the inside letters of wounds are used, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A person with open wounds also has internal injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal' keeps OUND, the inside of WOUNDS, and 'injuries' rearranges it. 'With' and 'has' are links; 'open' looks like part of the injury but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or button is to loosen it.

clue.text: Standing for the president to greet, is infirm

indicators.note: infirm means weak and unsteady, so these letters are in disarray

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frail man stands in for the president at a welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infirm' rearranges GREET IS into RESTIGE, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in the sense of status: high reputation and esteem.

clue.text: A kind letter

definitions.meaning: a sort or nature, as in the ... of a place
a written symbol, as in Chinese script

explanation.definitionFit: Character means a nature or sort, and also a written symbol such as an alphabetic sign.

clue.text: A travesty of a soft drink, based on tea?

indicators.note: in an across answer the drink sits after, based on, the tea

parts.note: char is a British slang word for tea
ade is a fruit-flavoured soft drink such as lemonade

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a fizzy drink that is really just tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR (British slang for tea) comes first, with ADE following it.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurd pretence or sham, a mere show.

clue.text: Translated and gave to

explanation.definitionFit: Rendered means put into another language, and also handed over as payment or service.

clue.text: Some bars don't

definitions.meaning: a few bars of music recurring in a song, a chorus
an instruction to hold back from doing something

explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical chorus, and also a verb meaning abstain or hold back.

clue.text: For once, rang and said something nice about

parts.note: ex means former, once upon a time
a bell that rang tolled

explanation.surface: Bells rang out on one occasion and someone was praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly, speak of with enthusiasm.

clue.text: A Teddy Girl?

parts.note: read not as a 1950s British fashion girl but as a female teddy, a girl among bruins

explanation.surface: A young woman of the 1950s British Teddy Boy fashion scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy Girls were the female counterparts of Teddy Boys, a 1950s British youth fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ursine animal, which a teddy toy depicts.

clue.text: Make his curl and wave

parts.note: a make of goods is a brand

indicators.note: letters that curl twist round out of their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairdresser instructs a man's hair to be curled and waved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curl' rearranges HIS into ISH after BRAND; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to flourish it about threateningly.

clue.text: Island that's no good to hide up in

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
good hides the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: A1 means excellent, good; the figure 1 is written as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island which is no use for anyone wanting to hide away.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (good, with 1 as I) hides NO to give ANOI, and 'up' reverses it to read upwards. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small isle of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, home to an ancient abbey.

clue.text: A second indication of one's satisfaction

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny moment in British speech, and a check mark showing something is correct.

clue.text: Certain I missed out Greek

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missed means left out, so a letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that they left out the Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops I from CERTAIN to leave CERTAN, and 'out' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Crete, the largest island of Greece.

clue.text: The nippers understand that half

parts.note: read as under-stand: a golf tee is the little stand the ball sits on

indicators.note: only the first half of the word that is used

explanation.surface: The children grasp half of what is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nippers' looks like children but means biters. 'understand' is read as 'under stand': a tee is the peg the golf ball stands on. 'half' keeps TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting parts of the mouth, which nip.

clue.text: The divider is for show

definitions.meaning: a partition separating parts of a room

explanation.definitionFit: A partition between spaces, and also a verb meaning to show a film or programme.

clue.text: Thinks bees, perhaps, live in it

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone supposes that bees may well dwell in a hive.
explanation.walkthrough: BEES plus LIVE rearranged; 'in it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of the opinion that something is true.

clue.text: Had looked about five, though older

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the letter

parts.note: had looked means had seen
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone appeared to be about five years old, though really older.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN goes about V. The definition is cryptic: the number just above five is older than five.
explanation.definitionFit: As an age, the next number but one after five is older than five.

clue.text: Rushed like crazy-the sea was going out

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: something going out is leaving its place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ran like mad because the tide was ebbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was going out' rearranges THE SEA into EHASTE, after MAD; 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurried, went quickly.
